source_text: Vides quidem etiam ipse rem dignam conflictatione non esse; tamen, ut mentibus subveniatur incautis, quae crassiores quasque opiniones et malis moribus blandientes in solacium assumunt conscientiae sauciatae, interrogamus, utrum tantae stoliditatis inventum de aliqua Scripturarum occasione compereris. Si dixeris: Per unum hominem peccatum intravit in mundum [n81] , admonemus te, ut relegas praesentis operis superiorem libellum, cuius si memor fueris, Apostoli testimonium usurpare non poteris.
pass_a_gloss: You yourself indeed see that the matter is not worthy of conflictation; nevertheless, that unwary minds may be helped, which take up cruder opinions and those flattering bad manners as solace of a wounded conscience, we ask whether you have found an invention of such stupidity from some occasion of the Scriptures. If you have said: Through one human sin entered into the world, we admonish you that you reread the superior little book of the present work, of which if you have been mindful you will not be able to usurp the Apostle's testimony.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Even you see that this is not worth disputing. Still, we must help unwary minds that seize on the crudest opinions, flattering bad conduct, to comfort a wounded conscience. We therefore ask whether you discovered any occasion in Scripture for an invention of such stupidity. If you say, ‘Through one man sin entered the world’ (Romans 5:12), we remind you to reread the preceding book of this work. If you remember it, you will be unable to appropriate the apostle’s testimony.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
